title: Critical Data Question 1
scenario: Imagine a giant ice cube floating in a glass of water. If that ice cube melts, the level stays the same.
question: Now think about Arctic sea ice floating in the ocean. If this floating sea ice melts completely, what happens to sea level?
options: It adds a lot of extra water to the ocean
The sea level stays about the same
The sea level will go down

title: Critical Data Question 2
scenario: Satellite records show Arctic sea-ice area shrinking in every recent decade.
question: What does less bright ice at the surface do to how much sunlight Earth absorbs?
options: Earth reflects more sunlight, so cooling increases
Earth absorbs more sunlight, which can amplify warming
It has no measurable impact on energy balance

title: Critical Data Question 3
scenario: Permafrost stores large amounts of frozen organic carbon across Arctic land.
question: When permafrost thaws, which climate effect is most likely?
options: Long-term greenhouse gas release can increase
Only ocean salinity changes, not climate

title: Critical Data Question 4
scenario: The Arctic warms several times faster than the global average.
question: Which action helps reduce future warming pressure the most?
options: Higher fossil fuel use for short-term growth
Reducing emissions through efficiency and clean energy
